questions.takeaway: With unmanaged compute like EC2, AWS keeps the hardware and the customer keeps each instance's OS.

read.text: Unmanaged, like EC2: AWS covers the physical layer, while each instance's OS, network setup and apps are yours to set up, secure and maintain.

questions.stem: A bike rental shop runs its booking app on Amazon EC2 instances. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task falls to the shop on EC2 that a fully managed service such as AWS Lambda would take off its hands?

options.text: Patching the guest operating system on each instance
options.why: On EC2 each instance's OS belongs to the shop, while under Lambda AWS patches that environment instead.

options.text: Writing and securing the booking app's own code
options.why: The app code and its security stay with the shop on EC2 and on Lambda alike, so nothing moves.

options.text: Replacing failed hardware in the host servers
options.why: AWS already runs the physical servers under EC2, so this task is not the shop's in either model.

options.text: Guarding the facilities that house the host servers
options.why: Physical security of the data centers is AWS's share under EC2 as well, so the shop never held it.

questions.takeaway: Client-side encryption scrambles data before it leaves the client, unlike server-side encryption, which the service performs.

read.text: Client-side encryption: encrypting data on the client before the server gets it.

questions.stem: Which description fits client-side encryption?

options.text: Data is encrypted by the storage service after it arrives
options.why: Encryption performed by the service once data arrives is server-side encryption.

options.text: Data is encrypted only while it crosses the network
options.why: Protecting data only during its trip across the network describes encryption in transit.

options.text: Data is encrypted by the sender before a server receives it
options.why: Client-side encryption scrambles data on the client, so it is already encrypted when the server gets it.

options.text: Data is hidden by limiting which users are allowed to list it
options.why: Limiting who can list data is access control, which leaves the data itself readable.

questions.takeaway: Lambda charges only for the compute time runs use, priced by allocated memory, so idle gaps cost nothing.

read.text: You pay for compute time only, per millisecond, priced by allocated memory.

questions.stem: A photo printing website runs an AWS Lambda function each time a customer uploads an image, and it sits idle between uploads. How is the website charged for this function?

options.text: By the compute time of each run, priced by memory
options.why: Lambda bills only for the time code runs, at a rate set by the memory given to the function, so idle gaps cost nothing.

options.text: By the time each instance runs, busy or idle
options.why: Billing for running instances whether busy or idle is how EC2 On-Demand works, not how Lambda charges for runs.

options.text: By a set monthly price for a server bundle
options.why: A predictable monthly bundle price is Lightsail's model, while Lambda has no server bundle to rent.

options.text: By the resources each container task uses
options.why: Paying for the resources containers use is Fargate's model, while Lambda bills each function run instead.

questions.takeaway: When a company lacks migration skills, AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners supply experts for each phase.

read.text: Competency partners fill expertise gaps.

questions.stem: A regional credit union wants to move its branch systems to AWS, but its IT staff have never moved systems to the cloud. It wants an outside firm with proven skill in the phase it is about to start. What should it do?

options.text: Engage one of the AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners
options.why: These AWS partners specialize in particular migration phases or needs, so one of them fills the credit union's missing expertise.

options.text: Post its open questions about the move on the AWS re:Post community site
options.why: re:Post is a community question and answer site, so it offers advice threads rather than a firm to run the move.

options.text: Read the articles and videos on common topics in the AWS Knowledge Center
options.why: The Knowledge Center holds articles and videos on common questions, which leaves the credit union without hands-on migration help.

options.text: Run the AWS Trusted Advisor best practice checks against its AWS account
options.why: Trusted Advisor checks an account against best practices and supplies no outside firm to lead a migration.

questions.takeaway: Cost optimization seeks the right balance of cost, performance and operational efficiency rather than the lowest price.

read.text: Aim for the right balance of cost, performance and operational efficiency.

questions.stem: A team is trimming the monthly bill of an AWS architecture. According to AWS guidance, which things should the team weigh against each other as it makes changes?

options.why: Cost work aims for the right mix of price, performance and operational efficiency, and good tweaks often help all three.

options.text: Compute, storage and outbound data transfer
options.why: These are the main cost drivers to examine, rather than goals to trade off against each other while making changes.

options.text: Pay as you go, commitments and volume tiers
options.why: These are the AWS pricing principles, which describe how services are charged rather than what to balance in a design.

options.text: Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations
options.why: These are parts of the global infrastructure where resources run, rather than the goals cost work balances.

questions.takeaway: Replacing a large upfront hardware cost with a bill that follows monthly use is trading fixed expense for variable expense.

read.text: On AWS the bill follows monthly usage, so you start small, spending matches consumption for more financial flexibility, and billing and budgeting tools help you save.

questions.stem: A furniture retailer would otherwise pay a large sum upfront for servers and floor space, then carry that cost through its slow months. On AWS, its bill instead rises and falls with what it uses each month. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud is this?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.why: Economies of scale lower unit prices through bulk buying, while the change here is in how the bill is shaped.

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
options.why: Swapping a big upfront outlay for a bill that tracks monthly use is trading fixed expense for variable expense.

options.text: Stop spending on data center upkeep
options.why: This benefit is about the ongoing upkeep of a facility, while the retailer's point is the upfront purchase.
Stop guessing capacity is about sizing resources to demand, while the retailer's point is how it pays.

questions.takeaway: AWS's huge purchasing volume cuts unit costs, and customers see those savings as lower prices.

read.text: Economies of scale: lower unit prices from huge purchase volumes.

questions.stem: Which explanation matches the economies of scale benefit of the AWS Cloud?

options.text: AWS bills each month for only the resources a customer actually used
options.why: A bill that follows usage is the variable expense benefit, which is about billing rather than AWS's buying power.

options.text: AWS buys hardware in huge volumes and passes the lower costs on
options.why: Huge purchase volumes lower AWS's unit costs, and those savings reach customers as lower prices.

options.text: AWS lets customers scale capacity with real demand instead of a forecast
options.why: Scaling with real demand is the stop guessing capacity benefit, which says nothing about AWS's purchase volumes.

options.text: AWS handles the racking, powering and cooling of its own data centers
options.why: Running the physical layer is the data center upkeep benefit, rather than lower prices from buying in bulk.

questions.takeaway: With pay-as-you-go pricing, charges end the moment a resource is deprovisioned, so a short-lived workload costs only its run time.

read.text: Billing for a resource ends the moment it is deprovisioned.

questions.stem: A museum runs an online exhibit on AWS for a few weeks and then shuts it down. Under pay-as-you-go pricing, why does the museum pay nothing for the exhibit after it closes?

options.text: Prices are lower because AWS buys hardware in bulk
options.why: Bulk buying lowers unit prices, but lower prices still add up while resources run, so it does not explain a zero bill.

options.text: Charges stop as soon as its resources are deprovisioned
options.why: Billing for a resource ends the moment it is released, so the exhibit costs nothing once its resources are gone.

options.text: Resources arrive within seconds whenever they are needed
options.why: Fast delivery explains how the exhibit could start quickly, not why the bill drops to zero after it closes.

options.text: Physical security of the data centers is handled by AWS
options.why: AWS does guard its data centers, but that security duty has no bearing on what the museum is billed.

questions.takeaway: Writing security group rules for your own instances is the customer's part of security in the cloud.

read.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, setting up network ACLs and security groups for your subnets and resources is your job.

questions.stem: An online bookstore runs its storefront on Amazon EC2 instances and wants only HTTPS requests to reach them. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who sets up the security group rules that do this?

options.text: The bookstore, as part of security in the cloud
options.why: Traffic rules around the bookstore's own instances are customer settings, so writing them is the bookstore's job.

options.text: AWS, as part of security of the cloud
options.why: Security of the cloud covers the hardware and facilities, not the rules a customer writes for its own instances.

options.text: AWS, since the filtering runs on its own network
options.why: AWS runs the filtering engine, but which requests the storefront accepts is a choice only the bookstore can make.

options.text: The bookstore and AWS, each writing half the rules
options.why: The model does not split one security group's rules between the parties; the customer owns all of them.

questions.takeaway: Rightsizing matches resource capacity to measured workload needs, so you stop paying for capacity that sits idle.

read.text: Rightsizing: measure real workload needs and resize to fit.

questions.stem: Which practice measures what a workload really uses and then changes its compute or database resources so their capacity matches that demand?

options.why: Rightsizing starts from measured demand and adjusts instance or database capacity to match it, cutting paid idle capacity.
Scaling up moves to a bigger resource for more power, which is a change in one direction rather than a fit to measured needs.
Lift-and-shift moves a workload to the cloud as it is, without measuring its use and adjusting its resources.
Provisioning just sets up resources, and on its own says nothing about matching their capacity to real use.

questions.takeaway: Windows shares that need SMB and Active Directory in AWS point to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.

read.text: FSx for Windows File Server: Windows Server storage with SMB, Microsoft Active Directory, data deduplication and steady sub-millisecond latency.

questions.stem: An architecture firm is moving the shared drives from its office servers into AWS. Its users reach those drives over SMB and sign in through Microsoft Active Directory. Which service fits?

options.why: EFS uses the Linux NFS protocol, so it does not serve SMB shares with Active Directory.
EBS gives one instance a block volume, with no SMB file sharing or Active Directory support.

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
options.why: It runs managed Windows Server storage in AWS with SMB and Active Directory, matching the firm's shares.
S3 File Gateway mainly bridges an on-site file share to S3, while the firm wants its servers running in AWS.

questions.takeaway: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is the cache built for DynamoDB to make its reads even faster.

read.text: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a built-in cache that sharply cuts DynamoDB read times.

questions.stem: Which option adds an in-memory cache built specifically for Amazon DynamoDB to cut the time its reads take?

options.why: DAX is the cache made for DynamoDB, and it sharply reduces how long DynamoDB reads take.
Global tables copy a table into other Regions, and they are not a cache in front of DynamoDB.
ElastiCache serverless is a general-purpose cache, not one built into DynamoDB itself.
Read replicas offload reads from an RDS database and have no role in DynamoDB.

questions.takeaway: To prove controls work with evidence gathered automatically, pick AWS Audit Manager.

read.text: Audit Manager is fully managed, audits usage continually and automates evidence collection across teams.

questions.stem: A mortgage lender must show outside examiners that its controls over customer funds work as intended. It wants the supporting proof gathered automatically and continuously across its teams. Which service fits?

options.why: Audit Manager automates evidence collection across teams and tests whether controls work, which is the proof the lender needs.
Artifact supplies reports on how AWS was audited, which proves nothing about the lender's own controls.
Config checks resource settings against rules, but gathering audit evidence about controls is Audit Manager's job.
CloudTrail records API calls that may feed an audit, but it does not collect and organize evidence for auditors.

questions.takeaway: Aligning IT with business strategy and measuring cloud investments, led by roles such as the CIO, is the AWS CAF Governance perspective.

read.text: Align IT and business strategy for more value and less risk; update skills and processes, measure cloud investments

questions.stem: The CIO of a water utility and its portfolio managers want IT and business strategy aligned to get more value with less risk. They also want to measure the results of each cloud investment. Which AWS CAF perspective fits?

options.why: Governance aligns IT and business strategy for more value and less risk and measures cloud investments, with the CIO as a typical role.
The Business perspective builds the business case for budget owners, while strategy alignment and portfolio oversight sit with Governance.
Operations runs and recovers workloads at agreed service levels, which is daily work rather than strategy alignment.
The Platform perspective designs architecture and the target state, a technical task rather than aligning strategy.

questions.takeaway: Central, organization-wide enforcement of firewall rules points to AWS Firewall Manager.

read.text: AWS Firewall Manager centrally configures and enforces firewall rules, such as AWS WAF rules, security group rules and AWS Network Firewall firewalls, across the accounts in your organization.

questions.stem: A car dealership group runs dozens of AWS accounts in one organization and wants the same AWS WAF rules and security group rules applied and enforced in all of them from one place. Which service fits?

options.why: Firewall Manager centrally configures and enforces firewall rules, such as WAF and security group rules, across an organization's accounts.
AWS WAF filters requests with the rules set up where it runs, but it does not roll rules out across accounts.
Shield Advanced defends against sophisticated DDoS attacks rather than managing rule sets across accounts.
Network Firewall is one kind of firewall that can be managed centrally; on its own it does not enforce rules in every account.

questions.takeaway: Slow loads for distant visitors call for CloudFront, which caches content at edge locations close to them.

read.text: CloudFront is a CDN (content delivery network) that securely serves static and dynamic web content from edge locations near customers, for faster loads, lower cost and reliability.

questions.stem: A recipe website hosts its photos and pages in a single AWS Region, but visitors on other continents complain that pages load slowly. Which service serves cached copies of the content from locations near those visitors?

options.why: CloudFront is a CDN that keeps copies at edge locations near visitors, so pages travel a shorter distance.
Route 53 turns the site's name into an address but stores no copies of photos or pages near visitors.
Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS network to healthy endpoints, but it does not cache site content.
Direct Connect is a private line from a data center to AWS and does nothing for public visitors far away.

questions.takeaway: A hands-on consulting project such as a security audit or complex migration calls for AWS Professional Services.

read.text: AWS Professional Services: project-based consulting, such as complex migrations, security audits and performance tuning.

questions.stem: A regional insurer wants a hands-on, project-based engagement in which AWS experts carry out a security audit of its environment. Which option fits?

options.why: Professional Services runs project-based consulting such as security audits, migrations and performance tuning.
Solutions architects advise on design and best practices, rather than running a full audit project.
The Trust and Safety Center takes reports of suspected abuse, rather than auditing a customer's setup.
Trusted Advisor runs automated checks against best practices, with no hands-on project led by AWS experts.

questions.takeaway: After a full first snapshot, each EBS snapshot stores only the changed blocks, which keeps backups fast and cheap.

read.text: The first snapshot is a full baseline of all blocks in use.

questions.stem: A news website takes an Amazon EBS snapshot of a large volume every night. Each nightly snapshot takes less time and adds less storage cost than the very first one did. What explains this?

options.text: Snapshots are kept in Amazon S3 across several Availability Zones
options.why: This is where snapshots live, and it says nothing about why later ones are quicker and cheaper than the first.

options.text: Each later snapshot stores only the blocks that changed
options.why: After a full first snapshot, each later one saves only changed blocks and points back to the earlier ones.

options.text: EBS replicates each volume within its Availability Zone
options.why: Replication inside the zone protects the live volume, and it does not shrink the work or cost of each backup.

options.text: One snapshot can be used to create many new volumes
options.why: Creating volumes from a snapshot is a way to use backups, and it does not explain why later backups cost less.

questions.takeaway: The console, the AWS CLI and the AWS SDK all work by calling the same AWS APIs.

read.text: Every AWS task, from launching to stopping or changing an instance, is an API request.

questions.stem: Whether a user clicks through the AWS Management Console, types an AWS CLI command or runs code built on an AWS SDK, how is a resource launch or change carried out underneath?

options.text: Each tool sends a request to an AWS API
options.why: Every action on AWS is an API request, and all three tools call the same APIs to carry it out.

options.text: Each tool can launch and stop Amazon EC2 instances
options.why: All three can launch and stop instances, but that says what they do, not how the change is carried out.

options.text: Each tool is free, and only the resources it creates are billed
options.why: The tools carry no charge of their own, but that does not explain how a change is carried out.

options.text: Each tool can work with resources in many AWS Regions
options.why: All three can reach many Regions, but that does not explain the mechanism underneath each change.

questions.takeaway: Notifying people at once by push, SMS or email points to Amazon SNS, while work processed later points to SQS.

read.text: SNS is publish-subscribe: publishers send a message to a topic, and subscribers such as web servers, email addresses and Lambda functions receive it.

questions.stem: A fitness app wants to tell its users right away, by mobile push and email, when a class they follow opens for booking. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: SNS pushes each message to topic subscribers at once and can fan out to people by mobile push and email.
SQS holds messages for a consumer to collect later and does not push them to people.
EventBridge routes events between applications and services rather than notifying people by push and email.
Kinesis Data Streams ingests streaming data for processing and does not send notifications to users.

questions.takeaway: A load balancer spreads incoming requests across instances so none sits idle or overloaded.

read.text: A load balancer receives incoming requests and decides which instance serves each one.

questions.stem: What does a load balancer do for a group of Amazon EC2 instances?

options.text: It takes incoming requests and picks an instance for each one
options.why: A load balancer receives each request and decides which instance serves it, so none is overloaded.

options.text: It adds and removes instances as demand rises and falls
options.why: Changing the instance count is the job of Auto Scaling, not of a load balancer.

options.text: It holds messages until an instance is ready to process them
options.why: Holding messages for later is what a message queue does, not a load balancer.

options.text: It gives running instances more CPU and memory when they are busy
options.why: Adding CPU and memory to an instance is vertical scaling, which a load balancer never does.

questions.takeaway: Independent audit reports on AWS itself come from AWS Artifact Reports, ready to hand to an auditor.

read.text: Reports: up-to-date outside audits of AWS against worldwide, regional and industry security rules, which you can show your auditors or regulators as proof.

questions.stem: A fintech startup's external examiner wants current third-party attestations showing how AWS itself meets security standards. Where can the startup download them?

options.why: Artifact Reports holds up-to-date third-party audits of AWS that the startup can download and pass to its auditor.
Artifact Agreements is for reading and accepting agreements with AWS, and it holds no audit reports on AWS itself.
Audit Manager builds reports on the startup's own controls, not independent audits of how AWS meets standards.
CloudTrail logs record API calls inside the startup's account, which says nothing about how AWS was audited.

questions.takeaway: Self-service business intelligence dashboards for non-technical users point to Amazon Quick Sight.

read.text: BI at scale: experts and non-experts build interactive dashboards and reports without infrastructure or developers; Amazon Q in QuickSight adds natural language

questions.stem: A chain of fitness studios wants its studio managers, who have no technical background, to create interactive dashboards and reports from membership and sales data. It wants no servers to run and no coding help. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Quick Sight is the business intelligence service where non-experts build interactive dashboards with nothing to host.
OpenSearch Service focuses on live search and monitoring of logs and operational data, not business reports.
Athena answers SQL queries over data in S3, which needs query skills and does not produce dashboards itself.
Redshift stores and queries warehouse data, but it is not the tool managers use to build their own dashboards.

questions.takeaway: Organization-wide change management, skills and staffing belong to the AWS CAF People perspective.

read.text: People owns change management; Platform owns architecture and moving workloads.

questions.stem: The HR lead at a hotel group must drive change management across the whole company, review roles and skill gaps, and set training and staffing priorities for the move to AWS. Which AWS CAF perspective guides this work?

options.why: The People perspective owns organization-wide change management and sets training, staffing and organizational priorities.
Governance aligns IT with business strategy and measures cloud investments, rather than leading change management.
Operations covers running and recovering workloads at agreed levels, rather than staffing and training across the company.
The Business perspective builds the business case and ranks cloud initiatives, rather than guiding people through the change.

questions.takeaway: AWS solutions architects give paying Support customers design and best practice advice for scalable, secure apps.

read.text: AWS solutions architects: for Business and Enterprise customers, help designing scalable, secure apps, with architecture and best practice advice.

questions.stem: A fitness app company on AWS Business Support+ wants AWS experts to advise it on the design and best practices for building a scalable, secure new app. Which AWS resource fits?

options.why: Solutions architects help paying Support customers design scalable, secure apps with design and best practice advice.
A designated TAM comes with AWS Enterprise Support, a higher plan than the one the company has.
The Trust and Safety Center takes reports of suspected abuse and gives no design advice.
The Knowledge Center offers FAQ articles and videos, rather than experts who advise on one company's design.

questions.takeaway: IAM denies by default, so a new identity can do nothing until a policy allows it.

read.text: Default deny is the mechanism: a new identity has zero permissions, not even to launch an EC2 instance or create an S3 bucket, until explicitly allowed.

questions.stem: A pet supply store creates a new IAM user for a stock clerk and attaches no policies to it yet. The clerk then tries to open an Amazon S3 bucket and is refused. Which IAM behavior explains the refusal?

options.why: IAM refuses every action until a policy allows it, so a user with no policies cannot open any bucket.
Least privilege guides what an admin chooses to allow; it is a principle, not the mechanism that refused this request.
A permission boundary caps the most an identity can hold, and none was set here, so it did not cause the refusal.
Role-based access control ties access to a person's job, which is a design choice and not what blocked the new user.

questions.takeaway: AWS runs the hypervisor that isolates instances sharing a host, so that isolation is AWS's responsibility.

read.text: A hypervisor on the host shares resources among them while isolating them, and AWS manages host, hypervisor and isolation.

questions.stem: An insurance broker worries that other customers' instances on the same physical host might reach its data. Which component keeps the instances on a host apart, and which party is responsible for it?

options.text: The hypervisor running on the host, which AWS manages
options.why: The hypervisor shares the host's resources while isolating each instance, and AWS is responsible for it.

options.text: The guest operating system, which the customer manages
options.why: The customer does manage the guest OS, but it runs inside one instance and cannot keep other tenants out.

options.text: The Amazon Machine Image, which the customer chooses
options.why: The customer does choose the AMI, but an AMI only sets what an instance starts with, not isolation on a host.

options.text: The Availability Zone of the host, which AWS operates
options.why: AWS does operate each zone, but a zone holds many hosts and does not keep the instances on one host apart.

questions.takeaway: A CloudWatch metric tracks a value over time, and custom metrics cover values AWS does not measure by itself.

read.text: Track a value per resource, built in (EC2 CPU) or custom

questions.stem: A print shop's ordering app on Amazon EC2 keeps a running count of pages each printer has produced, a value AWS has no built-in measure for. The shop wants that count tracked over time in Amazon CloudWatch. Which feature should it use?

options.why: A custom metric tracks a value AWS does not measure by default, such as the shop's page count, over time.
A dashboard displays metrics that already exist, so the page count must first be tracked as a metric to appear there.
An alarm reacts when a metric crosses a threshold, so it needs the page count tracked as a metric before it can act.
A trail records API calls made in the account, which says nothing about how many pages a printer produced.

questions.takeaway: Visibility, auditability and the choice of security controls, led by roles such as the CISO, belong to the AWS CAF Security perspective.

read.text: Visibility, auditability, control and agility; choose and implement security controls

questions.stem: Which AWS CAF perspective aims for visibility, auditability, control and agility in the cloud?

options.why: The Security perspective seeks visibility, auditability, control and agility and selects the controls to put in place.
Governance aligns IT with business strategy and measures cloud investments, rather than seeking auditability and control.
Operations defines the routines for running and recovering workloads, rather than auditability and control.
The Platform perspective designs architecture and the target state, which differs from choosing protective controls.

questions.takeaway: Finding the sentiment in large amounts of customer text with a ready-made model points to Amazon Comprehend.

read.text: Classifying, compliance, sentiment in lots of customer comments

questions.stem: An online furniture retailer receives a large volume of written product reviews every week. It wants to flag the reviews that express negative feelings without training a model of its own. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Comprehend applies pre-trained language analysis to text and reports its sentiment, so negative reviews stand out.
Polly reads text aloud as speech, which does nothing to judge whether a review is negative.
Textract pulls text out of scanned forms and documents, but the reviews are already text and need sentiment.
Rekognition analyzes images and video, while the retailer's reviews are written text.

questions.takeaway: Infrastructure as code keeps an environment as a versioned blueprint, so it can be rebuilt identically in any Region.

read.text: Infrastructure as code (IaC) stores the architecture as a source-controlled blueprint that tools rebuild anywhere, identically and easily.

questions.stem: Which approach declares what an entire environment should contain in files kept under source control, so tools can rebuild that environment identically in any Region?

options.why: Command-line scripts run commands step by step for routine jobs and grow hard to maintain, rather than declaring a whole environment.
Infrastructure as code declares the environment in source-controlled files that tools can rebuild identically anywhere.
Programmatic access calls AWS through code one step at a time, such as saving user data, not keeping a blueprint of a whole environment.
Console workflows suit newcomers and small one-off jobs, and they leave no declared definition that rebuilds the same way.

questions.takeaway: Encryption makes data unreadable to anyone who lacks the key that unlocks it.

read.text: Encryption is a lock: only holders of the right key can read data such as customers' phone and card details.

questions.stem: What does encrypting a set of data achieve?

options.text: It can be read only by holders of the right key
options.why: Encryption locks data so that only someone holding the correct key can unlock and read it.

options.text: It can never be turned back into readable form
options.why: Data that can never be restored describes one-way hashing, while encrypted data can be decrypted with its key.

options.text: It is hidden by swapping values for stand-in tokens
options.why: Swapping values for stand-ins is tokenization, which protects data without using encryption keys.

options.text: It is reachable only after a second sign-in factor
options.why: A second sign-in factor guards access to an account and does nothing to make the data itself unreadable.

questions.takeaway: A UDP flood forges the victim's address so a public service buries it in large replies.

read.text: Bots ask a helpful public service, like the National Weather Service, for forecasts, forging your address as the sender.

questions.stem: A florist's web server is swamped by large replies from a public lookup service it never contacted, because attackers sent that service small requests forging the florist's address. What kind of attack is this?

options.why: Forging the victim's address so a public service sends it large replies is how a UDP flood overwhelms a server.
SQL injection sends crafted input to a database query rather than drowning a server in unwanted replies.
Guessing passwords targets sign-in, while this server is swamped by replies it never asked for.
Phishing tricks people into giving up details and does not flood a server with traffic.

questions.takeaway: Processing data on secure, rugged hardware at a remote site is edge computing, which Snowball Edge devices also serve.

read.text: They bring strong compute, large capacity and gigabytes per second, and also serve rugged, secure edge computing.

questions.stem: A mining company runs a remote site in harsh conditions with no reliable network link. It needs secure, rugged hardware on site that processes sensor data where it is collected. Which type of workload is this?

options.why: Processing data on a secure, rugged device at a remote site is edge computing, a use case that Snowball Edge devices serve.
Serverless computing runs code in AWS Regions without managing servers, which needs the network link this site lacks.
A multi-cloud deployment spreads workloads across several cloud providers, rather than processing data on site.
A cloud-based deployment runs everything in the cloud, which a site without a reliable link has no way to reach.

questions.takeaway: A schema is a database's blueprint of tables, field types and relationships, and a new engine means recreating it.

read.text: Schema: The blueprint of a database's tables, field types and relationships.

questions.stem: In a relational database, what is the blueprint that defines the tables, the type of each field and the relationships between tables?

options.why: The schema is the database's blueprint of tables, field types and relationships, which is what the stem describes.
A stored procedure is a code object that runs logic inside the database, rather than the layout of its tables.
A read replica is a copy of a database that serves reads, so it holds data rather than defining the structure.
A partition key decides where a NoSQL item is stored and describes no tables or relationships.

questions.takeaway: Keeping existing licenses in use and in check on AWS, with usage caps and cost control, is the job of AWS License Manager.

read.text: License Manager tracks and controls those licenses and tunes their cost.

questions.stem: An engineering consultancy is moving its servers to AWS and plans to keep running database software whose usage rights it already bought from a vendor. It wants to track how much of that purchased capacity is in use and stop launches that would exceed its vendor contracts. Which service fits?

options.why: License Manager tracks the consultancy's own licenses, enforces usage caps and can block launches that would break the contract terms.
Service Catalog offers approved resources for staff to launch, but it does not count license use against a vendor contract.
Control Tower governs how accounts are set up across an organization, which says nothing about software license counts.
Cost Explorer shows AWS spending over time, but it cannot enforce limits on licenses the consultancy bought from a vendor.

questions.takeaway: CloudTrail event history is a free, ready-made view of recent management events in each Region.

read.text: Single actions (API or console calls); event history shows 90 days of management events per Region, free, searchable, downloadable, unchangeable

questions.stem: A small architecture firm wants to look up management actions taken in its account over the past few weeks in one Region. It wants to do this right away, with no setup and no extra charge. Which AWS CloudTrail feature fits?

options.why: Event history is available without setup and shows recent management events per Region for free, so the firm can search it now.

options.text: A trail sending logs to Amazon S3
options.why: A trail must be created first and stores logs in S3, so it only captures actions from the moment it starts.
Insights must be enabled and only flags unusual API volume or error rates, rather than listing the firm's recent actions.
Integrity validation proves delivered log files were left untouched, which does nothing to list recent account actions.

questions.takeaway: Tape backup software that should keep running against cloud storage points to Tape Gateway.

read.text: Tape Gateway: virtual tapes in Amazon S3 that backup software treats as tape hardware, with rarely used data movable to a cheaper class.

questions.stem: A school district's backup software writes each night to an on-site library of magnetic cartridges. The district wants to keep that software and its routine unchanged, but hold the backups in AWS instead of on site. Which option fits?

options.why: Cached mode presents iSCSI block volumes to local apps, which this backup software does not write to.
S3 File Gateway appears as a file share, while the backup software expects cartridge hardware.
Tape Gateway shows the software virtual tapes that it stores in Amazon S3, so the backup routine stays as it is.
Stored mode keeps block volumes on site and backs them up as EBS snapshots, which the software cannot use as a cartridge library.

questions.takeaway: S3 charges across several components, including storage, requests, transfer out, management, replication and Object Lambda processing.

read.text: S3 has six cost components: storage, requests and retrieval, transfer and acceleration, management and analytics, replication, and S3 Object Lambda processing.

questions.stem: A video archive company is estimating its monthly AWS charges for Amazon S3 alone. Which charges belong on that estimate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Data kept in storage over time
options.why: Storage is a core S3 cost component, charged for the data kept in buckets over time.
Replication is one of the S3 cost components, charged when objects are copied to another location.
Instance hours are charged by compute services such as Amazon EC2, and S3 runs no instances for the company.
Provisioned block capacity is charged by Amazon EBS, while S3 bills for the objects actually stored.
Database instance hours are charged by Amazon RDS, which is outside an estimate for S3 alone.

questions.takeaway: Expert security tips and articles from AWS come through the AWS Security Blog.

read.text: AWS Security Blog: expert tips.

questions.stem: Which AWS resource publishes articles in which AWS experts share tips on protecting workloads?

options.why: The AWS Security Blog is where AWS experts share security tips and guidance.
Security Documentation gives official guidance arranged by product, not a stream of expert tip articles.
Trusted Advisor runs automated checks on an account rather than publishing expert articles.
The Health Dashboard reports AWS events that affect an account, not security tips.

questions.takeaway: AWS Unified Operations is the plan with 24/7 workload monitoring and an incident response in under 5 minutes.

read.text: Unified Operations is the only plan that includes 24/7 workload monitoring.

questions.stem: A national airline wants AWS to monitor its workloads 24/7 and to have an Incident Management Engineer respond in under 5 minutes when a mission-critical system is down. Which Support plan provides this?

options.why: Unified Operations is the only plan with 24/7 workload monitoring, and its engineers respond in under 5 minutes.
Enterprise Support responds in under 15 minutes and lacks the 24/7 workload monitoring the airline wants.
Business Support+ responds in under 30 minutes and includes no workload monitoring.
Basic Support has no technical support cases, so it offers neither monitoring nor an incident response.

questions.takeaway: When finance needs a cost-backed business case before approving a migration, use Migration Evaluator.

read.text: A data-driven business case: current versus target state, a readiness plan, projected cloud costs

questions.stem: Before it approves a move to AWS, the finance team at a home goods retailer wants a data-driven business case. The case must compare the current and target states and project the cloud costs. Which service fits?

options.why: Migration Evaluator builds a data-driven business case with current versus target state and projected cloud costs.
Migration Hub is the central place to track migration tasks, rather than the source of a cost-backed business case.
Application Discovery Service inventories servers and their links for the plan, rather than projecting costs for finance.
Application Migration Service moves applications once the move is approved, which comes after the business case.

questions.takeaway: The Well-Architected Framework treats a working design as a starting point, because needs change and working is not the same as well built.

read.text: The framework aims past merely working, at secure, high-performing, resilient and efficient designs, with one consistent method for any workload.

questions.stem: An online bookstore has handled every order for a year on the same architecture, and nothing has gone down. Which reasons does the AWS Well-Architected Framework give for examining this design again? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The framework sorts its guidance into six pillars, from Operational Excellence to Sustainability.
options.why: The pillar structure is true of the framework, but it describes how the guidance is organized rather than why the bookstore's design needs another look.

options.text: Requirements change over time, so sizes and processes picked at launch need a fresh look.
options.why: The framework expects needs to change, so a design that fit last year should be resized, refined and trimmed of waste as the workload becomes clearer.

options.text: The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a free, self-service way to check a workload against the pillars.
options.why: The tool being free is true, but its price is not a reason the framework gives for examining a design that already runs.

options.text: The framework sets its bar at secure, resilient and efficient, which is higher than merely running.
options.why: A year without downtime shows the design runs, but the framework also asks whether it is secure, resilient and efficient, which still needs checking.

options.text: The AWS Well-Architected Tool lets a reviewer mark a question as not applicable to a workload.
options.why: Skipping questions is a true feature of the tool, but it explains how a review runs rather than why the bookstore should look at its design again.

questions.takeaway: Quick, disposable environments for trying ideas are the increase speed and agility benefit, which shortens time to market.

read.text: Teams spin up test environments, try ideas and delete failures so costs stop, shifting time from provisioning and deprovisioning to innovating and optimizing.

questions.stem: A video game studio wants its developers to launch a test environment for each new feature idea in minutes and delete it once the experiment ends. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud does this reflect?

options.why: Going global is about deploying near users in other parts of the world, while these environments stay internal.
Spinning up throwaway environments quickly and deleting failed experiments is the speed and agility benefit.
Stop guessing capacity is about matching production capacity to real demand, rather than fast experiments.

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.why: Economies of scale lower prices through bulk buying, which does nothing to speed up experiments.

questions.takeaway: Real-time work on a large dataset held in memory points to memory optimized instances.

read.text: Memory optimized: fast in-memory processing of large datasets, as in analytics and databases.

questions.stem: An analytics firm runs real-time queries over a very large dataset, and the work is fastest when the whole dataset stays in RAM rather than on disk. Which Amazon EC2 instance family fits best?

options.why: Memory optimized instances are built to process large datasets quickly in memory.
Storage optimized instances speed up access to local disks, while this work needs the data in memory.
Compute optimized instances add CPU power, but the bottleneck here is holding the dataset in memory.
General purpose instances balance resources and lack the large memory this dataset calls for.

questions.takeaway: A managed choice of foundation models behind one API for generative apps points to Amazon Bedrock.

read.text: Managed FMs from Amazon and startups (Claude, Stable Diffusion) via one API; test, tune, integrate

questions.stem: A legal services firm is building a production application that generates both text and images. Developers want to try foundation models from several providers through a single API, with no infrastructure to manage. Which AWS service fits?

options.why: Bedrock offers managed foundation models from Amazon and other providers behind one API, ready for production apps.
JumpStart is a model hub inside SageMaker AI for fast starts, not the managed one-API service for multimodal apps.
Q Business is a finished assistant that answers staff questions from company data, not a platform for building apps.
Q Developer suggests code to programmers, but it does not give an application access to many foundation models.

questions.takeaway: Data moving between a browser and a server is protected in transit by an SSL/TLS-encrypted connection.

read.text: SSL and its successor TLS use certificates to verify identity, then encrypt the connection.

questions.stem: A local newspaper's subscription page collects card details in a browser form and sends them to its payment backend. What keeps the card details protected on the way?

options.why: TLS verifies the server with a certificate and then encrypts the connection, which protects data while it travels.
A password policy strengthens how users sign in, but it does not encrypt anything moving across the network.
An extra sign-in factor protects account access and leaves the traffic itself unencrypted.

options.text: A hashed and salted copy of the number
options.why: Hashing is one-way, so the backend could never recover the card details it needs to charge.

questions.takeaway: AWS Config records resource configurations, tracks their changes and checks them against your rules.

read.text: AWS Config records configurations, tracks changes and checks them against your rules.

questions.stem: Which capabilities does AWS Config provide? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Gathering audit evidence automatically across teams
options.why: Collecting audit evidence automatically is the job of AWS Audit Manager, while Config evaluates resource settings.

options.text: Keeping a history of settings and each change made to them
options.why: Config keeps a record of each resource's settings and tracks every change to them over time.

options.text: Supplying outside assessments of AWS's own security
options.why: Outside assessments of AWS itself come from AWS Artifact, while Config looks at the customer's own resources.

options.text: Testing whether procedures and policies work as intended
options.why: Testing whether controls such as procedures work is the job of AWS Audit Manager rather than Config.

options.text: Letting staff review and accept agreements with AWS
options.why: Reviewing and accepting agreements with AWS happens in AWS Artifact Agreements, not in Config.

options.text: Judging resources against rules the company defines
options.why: Config evaluates resource settings against rules the company sets and reports which resources pass or fail.

questions.takeaway: AWS Budgets is the billing tool that alerts when spend nears or passes a limit you set.

read.text: Budgets and Cost Explorer both forecast, but only Budgets sends threshold alerts.

questions.stem: A dental practice group wants to be warned as soon as its monthly AWS spend gets close to a limit it has set. Which tool sends that alert?

options.why: Budgets lets the group set a custom limit and sends a warning as spend nears or passes it.
Cost Explorer charts and forecasts spend, but it sends no alert when a limit is near.
The Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deployment and never watches live spending.

options.text: AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard
options.why: The dashboard shows charges and a forecast for the month, but it raises no threshold alerts.

questions.takeaway: A balanced or not-yet-understood workload starts on general purpose instances.

read.text: General purpose: balanced, for web services, code repositories and unpredictable workloads.

questions.stem: Which Amazon EC2 instance family is the usual starting point for a workload whose main resource needs are still unknown?

options.why: General purpose instances balance CPU, memory and networking, which suits a workload that is not yet understood.
Compute optimized instances favor CPU, which only pays off once CPU is known to be the bottleneck.
Memory optimized instances are for large in-memory datasets, a need that has not been shown here.
Storage optimized instances are for heavy local disk access, a need that has not been shown here.

questions.takeaway: S3 uploads and DynamoDB table data are encrypted at rest by default, while EBS encryption is an option to turn on.

read.text: Amazon S3: new buckets have encryption configured, and uploads are encrypted at rest automatically.

questions.stem: An insurance broker keeps data in several AWS services and wants to know where AWS already encrypts the stored data at rest without any setup from its team. Which data is protected that way? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket
options.why: S3 sets up encryption on each new bucket, so every object the broker uploads is stored encrypted with no extra work.

options.text: Items stored in an Amazon DynamoDB table
options.why: DynamoDB protects every table with KMS-managed keys on its side, so stored items are already encrypted for the broker.

options.text: Snapshots taken of an Amazon EBS volume
options.why: EBS snapshots support encryption at rest, but the team has to choose it, so it is not already in place for them.

options.text: Files on an Amazon EC2 instance's boot volume
options.why: An EC2 boot volume is an EBS volume, which the team has to choose to encrypt, so its files are not protected without setup.

options.text: Records in a database installed on Amazon EC2
options.why: A database the broker installs on EC2 keeps its records on EBS volumes, which stay unencrypted until the team turns encryption on.

questions.takeaway: A heterogeneous migration changes the database engine, so the schema must be recreated and apps may need changes.

read.text: Heterogeneous: a new engine, such as legacy commercial to Amazon Aurora, which is harder and may need app changes.

questions.stem: A travel agency moves its database from a legacy commercial engine to Amazon Aurora. Which challenge comes with this type of move?

options.text: The schema must be recreated for the new engine
options.why: Moving to a different engine means rebuilding the schema of tables, field types and relationships, which is slow by hand.

options.text: The source must stay offline for the whole move
options.why: AWS DMS copies the data while the source stays live, so the database can keep serving the agency.

options.text: All data must ship to AWS on a physical device
options.why: A physical device suits sites with poor connectivity or huge volumes, and a change of engine has no bearing on that.

options.text: The target must run the same engine as the source
options.why: Aurora is a different engine from the commercial one, which is exactly what makes this move heterogeneous.

questions.takeaway: Cached copies near distant users come from edge locations, which sit outside Regions and cut latency.

read.text: Edge locations sit apart from Regions, in spots like Atlanta and Shanghai, and cache data, video and apps for higher transfer speeds and lower latency.

questions.stem: A fitness company streams workout videos from a single AWS Region to members on several continents. Members far from that Region report long buffering before each video starts. Which part of the AWS global infrastructure should hold cached copies of the videos closer to those members?

options.why: Availability Zones sit inside the Region and add resilience there, so they do not bring videos nearer to distant members.
Edge locations sit outside Regions near users and cache video, cutting latency and speeding up delivery to far-off members.
Outposts runs AWS services in a customer's own facility, not at caching sites spread out near members around the world.
GovCloud Regions add strict controls for US government workloads and do not cache content near members.

questions.takeaway: Renting servers as a service gives fast provisioning and lets a business drop capacity it no longer needs.

read.text: AWS keeps huge capacity running, so instances are usable within minutes.

questions.stem: A small online bookstore is weighing a purchase of its own servers against renting virtual servers on Amazon EC2. Its owner worries about waiting weeks for hardware and about paying for spare machines after the holiday rush ends. Which traits of renting compute as a service address these two worries? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Instances can be running within minutes of a request
options.why: AWS keeps capacity running, so the bookstore no longer waits weeks for hardware to arrive and be installed.

options.text: Unneeded instances can be released when demand drops
options.why: The bookstore is never locked into machines it no longer needs once the holiday rush is over.

options.text: Each instance runs an operating system the customer picks
options.why: Choosing the operating system is true of EC2, but it does nothing about hardware waits or spare machines.

options.text: The hypervisor on each physical host is managed by AWS
options.why: AWS does run the hypervisor, but that neither shortens hardware waits nor removes spare machines.

options.text: Instance types offer different mixes of CPU and memory
options.why: Instance types do vary, but choosing among them does not address either of the owner's worries.

questions.takeaway: AWS Service Catalog lets staff self-serve from a curated catalog of approved resources.

read.text: It lets you build, share and organize a curated catalog of approved resources, such as baseline networking and security tools for new accounts, for consistent governance.

questions.stem: A university's researchers keep asking the IT team which resources they may launch, and some guess at settings on their own. IT wants to offer a curated set of approved, preconfigured resources that researchers can launch themselves. Which service fits?

options.why: Service Catalog holds a curated catalog of approved resources that researchers can launch on their own with consistent settings.
Control Tower governs how accounts are created and policed, while choosing approved resources for self-service is Service Catalog.
License Manager tracks software licenses and their limits, which does not give researchers approved resources to launch.
The Marketplace sells third-party software, so it is no curated list of resources the university itself approved.

questions.takeaway: An Availability Zone is an isolated part of one Region, with its own power and networking, holding one or more data centers.

read.text: Availability Zone (AZ): an isolated location in a Region, with one or more data centers.

questions.stem: Which statements about Availability Zones are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Each one is a small site that caches content close to end users
options.why: Caching content near users is the role of edge locations, which are separate from Availability Zones.

options.text: Each one sits inside a single Region and never spans two
options.why: An Availability Zone always belongs to exactly one Region and never stretches across Regions.

options.text: Each one is a geographic area that is chosen near customers
options.why: A geographic area chosen near customers describes a Region, which is the level that holds the AZs.

options.text: Each one has its own power, networking and connectivity
options.why: Separate power and networking keep a problem in one Availability Zone from spreading to the others.

options.text: Each one groups three or more physically separate locations
options.why: Grouping three or more separate AZs is true of a Region, while an AZ itself holds one or more data centers.

questions.takeaway: Managing users on nodes across AWS and on-premises from one view, in support of least privilege, points to AWS Systems Manager.

read.text: AWS Systems Manager shows all your nodes, meaning connection points, across accounts, Regions, multi-cloud and hybrid setups in one view.

questions.stem: To control who can get onto its servers, a logistics firm wants to administer the user accounts on every node it runs, in AWS and in its own data center, from one view. Which service fits?

options.why: Systems Manager shows nodes across AWS and hybrid setups in one view and automates user management on them.
Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as passwords, but it does not administer user accounts across a fleet of nodes.
IAM Identity Center gives staff one login to AWS accounts and applications rather than handling the users on each server.
IAM controls identities and permissions for AWS itself, not the user accounts on servers in the firm's own data center.

questions.takeaway: Once planning is done, AWS Application Migration Service moves apps to AWS quickly, cheaply and with minimal downtime.

read.text: Apps replicated to AWS faster, for less and with minimal downtime, optionally modernized

questions.stem: A gaming studio has finished its migration plan and is ready to move its applications. It wants them replicated to AWS quickly, at lower cost and with minimal downtime. Which service fits?

options.why: Application Migration Service replicates applications to AWS faster, for less and with minimal downtime.
Application Discovery Service inventories servers before planning, and the studio's plan is already done.
Migration Evaluator builds the business case in the assess phase, rather than moving applications.
DataSync moves files and objects into AWS storage, rather than replicating whole running applications.

questions.takeaway: S3 Lifecycle uses transition actions to move aging objects to cheaper classes and expiration actions to delete them.

read.text: Transition actions move objects to another class at a set age, such as Standard-IA after 30 days or Glacier Deep Archive after a year.

questions.stem: A travel agency writes booking logs to S3 Standard. The logs are read often for 30 days and rarely after that, but they must come back quickly whenever someone asks for one. Regulators require the agency to keep each log for a year, and then it should be deleted. Which S3 Lifecycle actions fit this pattern? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A transition action that moves logs older than 30 days to S3 Standard-IA
options.why: A transition at that age moves the cooled-off logs to a cheaper class while keeping them quick to read.

options.text: A transition action that moves logs older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
options.why: Deep Archive takes hours to return data, which breaks the need to get a log back quickly.

options.text: An expiration action that deletes logs once they are a year old
options.why: An expiration action deletes objects for good when they are no longer needed, matching the one-year retention rule.

options.text: An expiration action that deletes logs once they are 30 days old
options.why: Deleting logs at that age throws away records that regulators require the agency to keep for a year.

options.text: A transition action that moves new logs to S3 Standard-IA right away
options.why: New logs are read often in their first 30 days, and Standard-IA charges for each retrieval, so moving them at once costs more.

questions.takeaway: A rush that comes at a known time suits predictive scaling, which adds capacity before demand arrives.

read.text: Dynamic scaling responds to demand in real time, and predictive scaling schedules capacity ahead of expected demand.

questions.stem: A city transit office's trip planner gets heavy use every weekday morning at about the same time. It wants Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to have extra instances running before the morning rush begins. Which approach fits?

options.why: Predictive scaling schedules capacity ahead of demand that is expected, such as a daily morning rush.
Dynamic scaling reacts once demand rises, so instances would arrive after the rush has started.
Vertical scaling enlarges one instance and does not add instances ahead of the rush.
Scaling in removes instances as demand falls, which is the opposite of preparing for a rush.

questions.takeaway: A shared ledger that several companies use to trace goods points to Amazon Managed Blockchain.

read.text: Amazon Managed Blockchain runs blockchain networks, such as a grocer's food-safety shipment tracking.

questions.stem: A seafood wholesaler and its partner fleets want a shared, tamper-evident ledger network that records each catch from the boat to the store for food-safety checks. Which AWS service runs this kind of network?

options.why: Managed Blockchain runs blockchain networks, which give the partners one shared and tamper-evident record of each shipment.
Neptune maps relationships in a graph, but it does not run a ledger network shared among companies.
DynamoDB is a key-value database owned by one account, not a ledger network run across partners.
DocumentDB stores JSON documents for one application and does not provide a shared ledger network.

questions.takeaway: IAM Access Analyzer shows who can reach your resources and refines IAM permissions toward least privilege.

read.text: It analyzes external access and checks policies against corporate security standards, so you can set, verify and refine permissions.

questions.stem: A nonprofit's security team wants to see which of its resources can be reached from outside its account and to trim permissions that go unused or are too broad. Which service fits?

options.why: Access Analyzer reviews external access and IAM policies and trims unused or broad access toward least privilege.
Trusted Advisor runs broad best-practice checks, but fine-grained review of IAM permissions needs Access Analyzer.
Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities, which is a different job from refining IAM permissions.
Config checks resource settings against rules, but it does not analyze who can reach resources or trim permissions.

questions.takeaway: Beyond DNS lookups, Route 53 registers and consolidates domains and runs health checks on endpoints.

read.text: It also runs health checks, registers new domains and takes over DNS records from other registrars, so all your domains live in one place.

questions.stem: Which tasks can Amazon Route 53 perform? (Select TWO.)

options.why: Route 53 can register domains and take over records from other registrars, keeping them in one place.
Route 53 runs health checks on endpoints so it can route users toward ones that respond.
Caching copies of content near users is the job of Amazon CloudFront, not the DNS service.

options.text: Filtering packets at a subnet edge
options.why: Checking packets as they cross a subnet edge is done by network ACLs inside the VPC.

options.text: Carrying traffic on a private line
options.why: A dedicated private line from a data center is AWS Direct Connect, not a DNS feature.

questions.takeaway: Automatic growth during a spike and shrinkage right after it is elasticity, not long-term scalability.

read.text: Elasticity reacts in the moment: resources scale out automatically when demand spikes and back in when it falls, so each moment costs only what it needs.

questions.stem: A ticketing website sees traffic surge for a short time whenever seats for a popular show go on sale, then fall back. The company wants capacity to grow during each rush and shrink right after it, with no staff stepping in. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud is this?

options.why: Elasticity adds resources automatically when a rush starts and removes them when it ends, so each moment costs only what it needs.
Scalability is long-term planning for growth, not automatic adjustment during each short sales rush.
Global reach is about serving users in many places, not about following short bursts of demand.
Economies of scale lower prices through AWS's size and do not grow or shrink the site's capacity.

questions.takeaway: Building the business case and tying IT spending to business results is the AWS CAF Business perspective.

read.text: IT serves business needs and IT spending ties to key business results; build the business case, rank cloud initiatives, align goals

questions.stem: At a national bookstore chain, the finance director wants each dollar of IT spending tied to key company results. She also needs a cost-justified case for funding that ranks which cloud projects go first. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this work?

options.why: The Business perspective ties IT spending to business results, builds the business case and ranks cloud initiatives.
Governance aligns IT and business strategy and measures cloud investments, but the business case and ranking sit with Business.
The Platform perspective covers architecture and target-state design, a technical concern rather than a business case.
The People perspective handles change management, skills and staffing, rather than ranking cloud projects.
